annotations.label: Coalition splits over the budget
annotations.text: The 1995 budget passed late after the 1994 election. In the autumn the coalition split over the 1996 budget and a snap election was held in December.

annotations.label: Late budget after long coalition talks
annotations.text: After the October 2006 election, Gusenbauer's grand coalition took office only in January 2007, and the 2007 budget passed late.

annotations.label: Ibiza affair brings down the government
annotations.text: Kurz lost a no-confidence vote in May. A caretaker cabinet under Brigitte Bierlein served until after the September snap election.

annotations.label: Five months to form a government
annotations.text: After the September 2024 election, two rounds of coalition talks failed. Stocker's three-party coalition took office in March 2025 and the 2025 budget passed late.

annotations.label: A year with no budget law
annotations.text: After the December 1987 election it took until May 1988 to form Martens' eighth government. No budget law for 1988 was passed.

annotations.label: 541 days without a government
annotations.text: After the June 2010 election, Leterme stayed on as caretaker until Di Rupo's coalition took office in December 2011.

annotations.label: Caretaker rule and provisional budgets
annotations.text: Michel's government resigned in December 2018. Caretaker governments ran the country through 2019 without a full-year budget.

annotations.label: Seven-month formation and a late budget
annotations.text: After the June 2024 election, De Wever's five-party coalition took office in February 2025. The 2025 budget passed late.

annotations.label: Protests bring down Borisov
annotations.text: Borisov resigned in February after mass protests over power prices. A caretaker cabinet served until the May snap election.

annotations.label: Three elections in one year
annotations.text: The April and July elections produced no government. Caretaker cabinets served until Petkov took office after the November vote.

annotations.label: Petkov government falls
annotations.text: The 2022 budget passed late, in February. Petkov lost a no-confidence vote in June and a caretaker cabinet ran the country to the October snap election.

annotations.label: Two more snap elections
annotations.text: Elections were held in June and October 2024, the sixth and seventh since 2021. Zhelyazkov's government took office in January 2025.

annotations.label: Voters approve a revised constitution
annotations.text: Voters approved a fully revised federal constitution in April 1999. Substantive laws passed rose from 31 to 53.

annotations.label: Pandemic laws
annotations.text: Parliament passed the COVID-19 Act in September 2020 to give the Federal Council's emergency measures a legal basis.

annotations.label: Makarios dies in office
annotations.text: President Makarios died in August 1977. Spyros Kyprianou served as acting president and was then elected to the office.

annotations.label: Late budget after early House election
annotations.text: House elections were brought forward to December 1985 after the two largest parties clashed with President Kyprianou. The 1986 budget passed late.

annotations.label: A 100 to 100 parliament
annotations.text: The June 2006 election split the chamber 100 to 100. Topolánek's first cabinet lost a confidence vote and stayed on as caretaker into 2007.

annotations.label: Nečas falls, snap election
annotations.text: Nečas resigned in June 2013 over a scandal. Rusnok's appointed cabinet lost a confidence vote and an early election followed in October.

annotations.label: Minority cabinet without confidence
annotations.text: Babiš's first cabinet lost a confidence vote in January 2018 and governed as caretaker until his second cabinet won confidence in July.

annotations.label: Change of government after election
annotations.text: After the October 2025 election Fiala's cabinet stayed on until Babiš was appointed prime minister on 9 December.

annotations.label: Kohl replaces Schmidt
annotations.text: Schmidt's coalition broke up in September 1982. Kohl won a constructive no-confidence vote in October and called an early election for March 1983.

annotations.label: Six months to form a coalition
annotations.text: After the September 2017 election, Merkel's fourth cabinet took office in March 2018, and the 2018 budget passed in July.

annotations.label: Court ruling delays the budget
annotations.text: The Constitutional Court struck down a €60bn fund transfer in November 2023, so the 2024 budget passed only in February. The coalition broke up in November.

annotations.label: Snap election and a budget in September
annotations.text: After the February 2025 snap election, Merz took office in May. The 2025 budget passed in September.

annotations.label: New constitution and two elections
annotations.text: Voters approved a new constitution in May 1953. Elections were held in April and September, and Hedtoft replaced Eriksen as prime minister.

annotations.label: Budget defeat forces an election
annotations.text: Schlüter's minority government lost the budget vote in December 1983 and called an election for January 1984. The budget then passed late.

annotations.label: Late budget after snap election
annotations.text: After the November 2022 snap election, Frederiksen's new cross-bloc coalition took office in December, and the 2023 budget passed late.

annotations.label: Coalition talks after the March election
annotations.text: After the March 2019 election, Ratas formed a new three-party coalition, which took office at the end of April.

annotations.label: Ratas resigns, Kallas takes over
annotations.text: Ratas resigned in January 2021 over a corruption investigation in his party. Kaja Kallas formed a new coalition later that month.

annotations.label: Budget defeat and snap election
annotations.text: Parliament rejected the 1996 budget in late 1995. González called an early election for March, and Aznar took office in May.

annotations.label: Ten months without a government
annotations.text: After the December 2015 and June 2016 elections, Rajoy governed as caretaker until he won an investiture vote in October.

annotations.label: Two general elections in one year
annotations.text: Sánchez called an April election after his budget was rejected. No investiture followed, so a second election was held in November.

annotations.label: Budgets rolled over again
annotations.text: After the July 2023 snap election and Sánchez's November investiture, no 2024 or 2025 budget was passed. The 2023 budget was extended.

annotations.label: Caretaker cabinet and early election
annotations.text: Tuomioja's caretaker cabinet served until after the early election in March 1954. Two new cabinets followed that year.

annotations.label: Most of the year under caretakers
annotations.text: Lehto's non-party caretaker cabinet governed from December 1963 until Virolainen formed a coalition in September 1964.

annotations.label: Caretaker cabinet and early election
annotations.text: Sorsa's coalition broke up in 1975. Liinamaa's caretaker cabinet governed through the September early election until Miettunen took office in November.

annotations.label: Long coalition talks after election
annotations.text: After the April 2023 election, Orpo's four-party coalition took office in June, after about ten weeks of talks.

annotations.label: Dissolution delays the budget
annotations.text: De Gaulle dissolved the Assembly after it censured Pompidou in October 1962. The spending part of the 1963 budget passed only in February.

annotations.label: Budget law annulled
annotations.text: The Constitutional Council struck down the 1980 finance law in December 1979 on procedural grounds. A special law covered the gap until a new law passed in January.

annotations.label: Dissolution and three prime ministers
annotations.text: Macron dissolved the Assembly after the June European elections. Attal, Barnier and Bayrou each led governments during the year.

annotations.label: Budget via special law
annotations.text: Barnier's government fell to a censure vote in December 2024. A special law kept the state running until the 2025 budget passed in February.

annotations.label: Two elections, no majority
annotations.text: Elections in June and November 1989 gave no party a majority. Short coalition and caretaker cabinets followed.

annotations.label: A majority after three elections
annotations.text: A third election in April 1990 gave Mitsotakis a one-seat majority. In 1991 the budget was on time and there were no early elections.

annotations.label: Two elections in six weeks
annotations.text: The May 2012 election produced no government. A second election in June led to Samaras's coalition.

annotations.label: Two elections and a bailout referendum
annotations.text: Tsipras won the January 2015 election, held a bailout referendum in July, resigned in August and won again in September.

annotations.label: Late budget after change of government
annotations.text: After the November 2003 election, Sanader's government took office in December, and the 2004 budget passed late.

annotations.label: Government falls within six months
annotations.text: Orešković's government took office in January and passed a late budget. It lost a no-confidence vote in June, leading to a September snap election.

annotations.label: Snap election in April
annotations.text: Parliament was dissolved in March and an election held in April 2024. Plenković formed a new coalition in May.

annotations.label: Change of government after election
annotations.text: Orbán's Fidesz-led coalition replaced Horn's government after the May 1998 election. Law output fell that year.

annotations.label: Gyurcsány resigns, Bajnai takes over
annotations.text: Gyurcsány announced his resignation in March 2009. Bajnai took office in April through a constructive no-confidence vote.

annotations.label: New constitution and a burst of laws
annotations.text: With a two-thirds majority, Fidesz adopted a new constitution in April 2011 and passed many related laws.

annotations.label: Three elections in 18 months
annotations.text: Elections were held in June 1981, February 1982 and November 1982 as minority governments fell in turn.

annotations.label: Bailout and early election
annotations.text: Cowen's coalition broke up after the EU-IMF bailout. An early election in February 2011 brought Kenny to power.

annotations.label: 70 days to form a minority government
annotations.text: The February 2016 election left no majority. Kenny's minority government took office in May with Fianna Fáil support.

annotations.label: Four months to form a coalition
annotations.text: After the February 2020 election, Varadkar stayed on as caretaker until Martin's three-party coalition took office in June.

annotations.label: Two elections to change the voting system
annotations.text: Elections were held in June and October 1959 to adopt a new system of constituencies. The budget passed late.

annotations.label: Banking collapse and early election
annotations.text: Haarde's government fell in January 2009 after protests over the banking collapse. An early election followed in April.

annotations.label: Panama Papers and early election
annotations.text: Gunnlaugsson resigned in April 2016 after the Panama Papers leak. An early election was held in October.

annotations.label: Two prime ministers and a snap election
annotations.text: Jakobsdóttir resigned in April 2024 to run for president. Benediktsson's coalition collapsed in October and an election followed in November.

annotations.label: Caretaker government for most of the year
annotations.text: After the April 1963 election, Leone led a short holding government until Moro formed the first centre-left cabinet in December.

annotations.label: Early election after Andreotti falls
annotations.text: Andreotti's government lost its majority in early 1979. An early election was held in June and Cossiga took office in August.

annotations.label: Tangentopoli and electoral reform
annotations.text: Bribery investigations broke the old parties. Ciampi's government passed a new electoral law, and provisional budgets ended.

annotations.label: Prodi loses confidence vote
annotations.text: Prodi lost a Senate confidence vote in January 2008. An early election was held in April and Berlusconi returned.

annotations.label: Brazauskas government falls
annotations.text: Brazauskas's coalition collapsed and he resigned in mid-2006. Kirkilas formed a new government in July.

annotations.label: Change of government after election
annotations.text: The Social Democrats won the October 2024 election. Paluckas's government took office in December.

annotations.label: Paluckas resigns
annotations.text: Paluckas resigned at the end of July 2025 amid investigations into his business interests. Inga Ruginienė succeeded him.

annotations.label: Spy scandal ends Juncker's tenure
annotations.text: Juncker resigned in July 2013 over the intelligence service scandal. An early election in October led to Bettel's coalition.

annotations.label: Budget waits for the new coalition
annotations.text: Bettel's government took office in December 2013, and the 2014 budget passed late, in the spring.

annotations.label: Budget passes after October election
annotations.text: Because of the October 2018 election, the 2019 budget was passed late, in the spring.

annotations.label: Budget passes after October election
annotations.text: After the October 2023 election Frieden's coalition took office in November, and the 2024 budget passed late, in the spring.

annotations.label: President dissolves parliament
annotations.text: Zatlers called a referendum after the Saeima blocked a search of an MP's home. Voters approved dissolution and an early election was held in September.

annotations.label: Three months to form a government
annotations.text: After the October 2018 election, Kariņš took office in January 2019, and the 2019 budget passed late.

annotations.label: Late budget and a new prime minister
annotations.text: The 2023 budget passed late after the October 2022 election. Kariņš resigned in August and Siliņa took office in September.

annotations.label: Late budget after change of government
annotations.text: Labour won the October 1996 election, and the 1997 budget passed late.

annotations.label: One-seat majority fails
annotations.text: Sant called an early election after Dom Mintoff voted against the government. Fenech Adami returned to office in September 1998.

annotations.label: Budget defeat forces an early election
annotations.text: Gonzi's budget was voted down in December 2012. Muscat won the March 2013 election and the 2013 budget passed late.

annotations.label: 208 days of coalition talks
annotations.text: After the May 1977 election, Den Uyl stayed on as caretaker until Van Agt's cabinet took office in December.

annotations.label: Cabinet falls over Afghanistan mission
annotations.text: Balkenende's fourth cabinet fell in February 2010. After the June election, Rutte's first cabinet took office in October.

annotations.label: Benefits scandal and record formation
annotations.text: Rutte's third cabinet resigned in January 2021 over the childcare benefits scandal. Forming the next cabinet took a record 299 days.

annotations.label: Cabinet fall and long formation
annotations.text: Rutte's fourth cabinet fell in July 2023 over asylum policy. After the November election, Schoof's cabinet took office in July 2024.

annotations.label: Kings Bay affair
annotations.text: Gerhardsen's government lost a no-confidence vote in August 1963 after a mining accident. Lyng governed for a month before Gerhardsen returned.

annotations.label: Three prime ministers in one year
annotations.text: Nordli resigned in February 1981 and Brundtland took over. Willoch formed a Conservative government after the September election.

annotations.label: Willoch falls over fuel tax
annotations.text: Willoch lost a confidence vote on a fuel tax rise in spring 1986. Brundtland formed her second government.

annotations.label: Suchocka loses confidence vote
annotations.text: Suchocka's government lost a no-confidence vote by one vote in May 1993. Wałęsa dissolved parliament and an early election was held in September.

annotations.label: Miller resigns after EU accession
annotations.text: The 2004 budget passed late. Miller resigned in May 2004, the day after Poland joined the EU, and Belka took over.

annotations.label: Coalition collapse and early election
annotations.text: Kaczyński's coalition broke up and the Sejm voted to dissolve itself. Tusk won the October 2007 early election.

annotations.label: Change of government after election
annotations.text: After the October 2023 election, Morawiecki's third cabinet lost its confidence vote and Tusk took office in December.

annotations.label: Balsemão resigns, early election
annotations.text: Balsemão resigned in December 1982 and parliament was dissolved. After the April 1983 election, Soares formed a Socialist and PSD coalition.

annotations.label: Central Bloc coalition collapses
annotations.text: The PSD left the governing coalition in 1985. Cavaco Silva formed a minority government after the October early election.

annotations.label: Budget rejected, snap election
annotations.text: Parliament rejected the 2022 budget in October 2021. After the January 2022 election, the budget took effect only at mid-year.

annotations.label: Back-to-back snap elections
annotations.text: Costa resigned in November 2023. Elections followed in March 2024 and, after Montenegro lost a confidence vote, again in May 2025.

annotations.label: Ciorbea government replaced
annotations.text: Ciorbea resigned in March 1998 amid coalition disputes, and Vasile took over. The 1998 budget passed late.

annotations.label: Late budget, then a no-confidence vote
annotations.text: The 2009 budget passed late after the November 2008 election. Boc's government lost a no-confidence vote in October 2009.

annotations.label: Ruling party ousts its own government
annotations.text: Grindeanu took office in January 2017. His own party brought him down in a no-confidence vote in June, and Tudose replaced him.

annotations.label: Government resigns after presidential vote
annotations.text: Ciolacu resigned in May 2025 after the coalition candidate lost the presidential first round. Bolojan took office in June.

annotations.label: Pension dispute forces extra election
annotations.text: Erlander called an extra election in June 1958 after parliament rejected his pension reform.

annotations.label: 134 days to form a government
annotations.text: The September 2018 election left neither bloc a majority. Löfven stayed on as caretaker until January 2019.

annotations.label: Prime minister loses no-confidence vote
annotations.text: Löfven lost a no-confidence vote in June 2021 and was voted back in July. Andersson succeeded him in November.

annotations.label: Two changes of government
annotations.text: Drnovšek's coalition broke up and Bajuk took office in June 2000. Drnovšek returned after the October election.

annotations.label: Pahor loses confidence vote
annotations.text: Pahor's government lost a confidence vote in September 2011. Slovenia held its first early election in December.

annotations.label: Bratušek resigns, early election
annotations.text: Bratušek resigned in May 2014 after losing her party leadership. An early election was held in July and Cerar took office in September.

annotations.label: Cerar resigns, early election
annotations.text: Cerar resigned in March 2018 after the Supreme Court annulled a rail referendum. After the June election, Šarec took office in September.

annotations.label: Mečiar ousted, then returns
annotations.text: Mečiar lost a no-confidence vote in March 1994 and Moravčík took over. Mečiar returned after the autumn early election.

annotations.label: Government falls over euro rescue fund
annotations.text: Radičová tied a confidence vote to the euro rescue fund in October 2011 and lost. An early election followed in March 2012.

annotations.label: No-confidence vote and early election
annotations.text: Heger's government lost a no-confidence vote in December 2022. Ódor's appointed cabinet served until the September 2023 early election.

annotations.label: Two elections in one year
annotations.text: The February 1974 election produced a hung parliament. Wilson formed a minority government and won a small majority in October.

annotations.label: Snap election loses the majority
annotations.text: May called an early election for June 2017 and lost her majority. She governed with DUP support.

annotations.label: Brexit deadlock and early election
annotations.text: Parliament rejected May's Brexit deal three times. Johnson replaced her in July and won a December early election.

annotations.label: Three prime ministers in one year
annotations.text: Johnson resigned in July 2022. Truss took office in September and was replaced by Sunak in October.
